items.summary: “I see” IC 342, the Hidden Galaxy! Today’s image peers through the plane of the Milky Way, through all its gas, dust and stars, to unveil this spiral galaxy. IC 342 (or Caldwell 5) is one of the brightest members of the IC 342/Maffei group of galaxies. Located about 10 million light years away, this group is quite close to the Local Group that includes our Milky Way. Inaccurate accounting of the crowded and dusty Milky Way foreground has led to misunderstandings in IC 342’s history, including the theory that the galaxy was ejected from the Local Group. IC 342 has its own dust intermittently blocking the glow of hydrogen gas, indicating the presence of bright, young stars.

items.title: Nationwide trends in physical disability among rheumatoid arthritis patients in Korea (2010–2022): A retrospective cohort study based on national registry data
items.summary: by Bo Young Kim, Ji-Won Kim, Hwajeong Lee, Jung-Yoon Choe, Sung-Hoon Park, Sang Gyu Kwak Background Whether the burden of legally certified disability among patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) has decreased in the modern treatment era is uncertain, particularly in Asia. We investigated trends in registered and physical disability among Korean patients with RA. Methods Using National Health Insurance Service data (patient-level 50% random sample), we identified patients aged ≥19 years with seropositive RA registered in the copayment assistance program for rare and intractable diseases in 2010–2022. Disability status, including physical disability (certified musculoskeletal impairment), came from the national disability registry.
items.author: Bo Young Kim, Ji-Won Kim, Hwajeong Lee et al.

items.title: Structural characteristics and policy differences of digital health management policies in China: A quantitative analysis based on the PMC index model
items.summary: by Tong Lyu Digital health governance increasingly relies on policy systems that coordinate data resources, information platforms, standards, service delivery, regulation, security, innovation, and implementation support. However, the structural composition and cross-policy heterogeneity of China’s national digital health policy system remain insufficiently quantified. This study develops a domain-specific Policy Modeling Consistency (PMC) framework to evaluate the structural coverage of national-level digital health management policies in China. Using a source-locked corpus covering 2016–2025, 42 eligible policies were identified, of which 39 with complete and auditable texts were included in the quantitative analysis. The framework comprises nine dimensions and 48 binary indicators, generating 1,872 policy-by-indicator coding decisions.
items.author: Tong Lyu

items.title: Integrative analysis reveals shared biomarkers and pathways in osteoporosis and rheumatoid arthritis using machine learning and single-cell sequencing
items.summary: by Jin Zhao, Yixuan Chen, Fei Yang, Cheng Tian, Wenyan Luo, Zhou Su, Bohuan Yang, Wei Liu, Hongbo Yang Background Osteoporosis (OP) and Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) are prevalent chronic diseases characterized by bone loss and immune dysregulation. Evidence suggests that patients with RA are at increased risk of developing OP; however, the shared molecular mechanisms linking these conditions remain incompletely understood. Methods Publicly available bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets for OP and RA were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was applied to identify shared gene modules associated with both diseases.
items.author: Jin Zhao, Yixuan Chen, Fei Yang et al.

items.title: Treadmill prehabilitation attenuates jejunal inflammation and enhances cytoprotective protein expression in murine gut ischemia–reperfusion
items.summary: by Kazuya Higashizono, Kazuya Takahashi, Kazuhiko Fukatsu, Tomonori Narita, Haruka Takayama, Midori Noguchi, Satoshi Murakoshi, Yasuyuki Seto Introduction Whether preoperative exercise protects the intestine itself is unclear. We hypothesized that treadmill prehabilitation acts on the intestine as ischemic preconditioning, and examined intestinal injury and cytokine responses after gut ischemia–reperfusion (I/R) and jejunal cytoprotective protein expression before ischemia. Methods Two experiments were conducted in male C57BL/6J mice. In Experiment 1, mice were randomly allocated to a sedentary or an exercise group; exercised mice completed 1 week of acclimation and 3 weeks of treadmill running. One day after the final session, the superior mesenteric artery was occluded for 45 min.
items.author: Kazuya Higashizono, Kazuya Takahashi, Kazuhiko Fukatsu et al.

items.title: Spatial accessibility and equity of emergency medical services: Evidence from Ningbo
items.summary: by Minxia Fu, Jieyi Guan, Yixi Zheng, Xingchuan Gao, Wenwan Jin, Pengtao Wang Background Timely access to emergency medical services (EMS) is essential for improving survival outcomes and public health. In rapidly urbanizing Chinese cities, disparities in EMS accessibility are increasingly shaped by the spatial distribution of hospitals, population concentration, transport infrastructure, and built environment conditions. However, relatively few studies have simultaneously compared emergency and non-emergency medical accessibility and examined their spatial equity and influencing factors in medium-sized coastal cities. This study evaluates the spatial accessibility, equity, and clustering characteristics of EMS in Ningbo, China, and identifies the key built environment factors influencing these patterns.
items.author: Minxia Fu, Jieyi Guan, Yixi Zheng et al.

items.title: Simple and multiplexed tracking of bacterial growth in double emulsion droplets
items.summary: by Sebastián Somolinos Cedeño, Samuel Thompson, Polly Fordyce, Drew Endy Droplet-based microfluidics enable researchers to observe phenotypic heterogeneity within complex biological mixtures through parallel encapsulation of individual samples followed by imaging. Observing or quantifying dynamic heterogeneity remains challenging due to complexities associated with trapping and tracking many individual droplets. Current approaches for time-lapse imaging require specialized devices with droplet traps that limit accessibility and throughput. Here, using readily available materials and software, we demonstrate a simple method for stabilizing and monitoring many, individual droplets for up to 12 hours. We leveraged our method to track bacterial growth within droplets in a high-throughput manner for over 6 hours.
items.author: Sebastián Somolinos Cedeño, Samuel Thompson, Polly Fordyce et al.

items.title: Metagenomic analysis of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes detects Ralstonia phage sequences in Kenyan agricultural soils
items.summary: by Derleen Bosibori Mogire, Johnstone Neondo, Christabel Muhonja, Consolate Awuor, Daniel Mureithi, Stephen Ogada, Tofick Barasa Wekesa Bacterial wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum species complex is a major constraint in tomato production in Kenya, resulting in yield losses of up to 100% in heavily infested fields. This study used high-throughput shotgun metagenomic sequencing approach to characterize the rhizosphere microbiomes of tomato plants in three of the major production areas in Kenya (Kirinyaga, Kiambu, and Laikipia counties) focusing on detecting Ralstonia phage sequences. Soil samples were collected from the rhizosphere of bacterial wilt-infected tomato plants, and microbial DNA was extracted using a modified phenol-chloroform protocol and sequenced using Illumina NovaSeq platform.
items.author: Derleen Bosibori Mogire, Johnstone Neondo, Christabel Muhonja et al.

items.title: Mothers’ experiences of caring for a child with acute lymphoblastic leukemia in the West Bank, Palestine: A qualitative study
items.summary: by Baraa Ghalib Yassin Taqatqa, Kawther Elissa, Amani Salim, Salam Khatib Background Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) is the most common childhood cancer globally and requires prolonged, intensive treatment that places substantial demands on families. Mothers often assume primary caregiving roles; however, their experiences in conflict-affected settings remain underexplored. Objective This study aimed to explore the experiences of Palestinian mothers caring for a child diagnosed with ALL in the West Bank. Methods A qualitative descriptive study included fifteen mothers of children diagnosed with ALL and receiving treatment at Beit Jala Governmental Hospital, who were recruited using purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, transcribed verbatim and analyzed using qualitative content analysis following the approach of Graneheim and Lundman (2004).
items.author: Baraa Ghalib Yassin Taqatqa, Kawther Elissa, Amani Salim et al.

items.title: SEQuential tUnneled Catheters and Infective Events in haemodiaLysis: A Five-Year Retrospective Cohort Study (SEQUEL Study)
items.summary: by Shing Shen Bay, Suek Xuan Pon, Xin Yu See, Soo Ying Yew, Elisya Liyana Abdullah, Khai Vern Poon, Chee Keong Thye, Shian Feng Cheng, Yee Wan Lee, Maisarah Jalalonmuhali, Wan Ahmad Hafiz Wan Md Adnan, Chye Chung Gan Background Tunnelled-cuffed catheters (TCCs) are widely used for haemodialysis access when permanent vascular access is unavailable. Internal jugular vein (IJV) placement is guideline-preferred, but femoral vein (FV) catheters are frequently used when upper venous access is limited. Whether femoral access confers a higher infection risk than catheter sequence number remains unclear. This study evaluated these two competing determinants of catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI).
items.author: Shing Shen Bay, Suek Xuan Pon, Xin Yu See et al.

items.title: Defining and predicting outcomes of a work-injuries rehabilitation program through multivariate baseline phenotypes and longitudinal modeling
items.summary: by Mohammad Bayattork, Tom Carter, David M. Walton Objective To characterize short-term pain and health-related quality-of-life (HRQoL) recovery trajectories in injured workers undergoing standardized musculoskeletal rehabilitation. We also examined whether multidimensional baseline phenotypes derived from brief self-report measures predicted these trajectories and subsequent recovery. Methods Adults with work-related musculoskeletal injuries were enrolled at entry into a community-based rehabilitation program (N = 146), of whom 134 contributed to pain and 138 to HRQoL trajectory analyses. Participants were classified into one of 4 latent profiles at intake from a prior analysis: Localized/Resilient (57.0%), Mood-Dominant (21.8%), Neurosensory-Dominant (12.7%), and Complex/Central (8.5%). Pain (Numeric Pain Rating Scale, NPRS) and HRQoL (EQ-5D-5L index) were measured at baseline, 4, and 8 weeks; self-rated global recovery, self-reported return-to-work status, and administrative discharge/ongoing-care codes were collected at 8 weeks.
items.author: Mohammad Bayattork, Tom Carter, David M. Walton

items.title: Identification and validation of biomarkers associated with mitochondrial dynamics dysfunction in Parkinson’s disease based on GEO datasets
items.summary: by Dawei Gong, Guanyu Li, Ming Li, Bo Zhang, Weixiao Wang, Jinjin Chen, Yanyan Zhao Background Parkinson’s disease (PD), the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder, is characterized by an unclear etiology and a lack of specific early diagnostic biomarkers. This study investigated novel biomarkers associated with mitochondrial dynamics (MD) dysfunction in PD. Methods Transcriptomic data from the Gene Expression Omnibus database (training set: GSE6613, n = 72; validation set: GSE99039, n = 438) and 23 MD-related genes (MDRGs) were integrated. Differentially expressed genes were screened using the limma package. Three machine learning algorithms (random forest, support vector machine, and generalized linear model) were employed to construct diagnostic models.
items.author: Dawei Gong, Guanyu Li, Ming Li et al.

items.title: Academic entitlement and student well-being: The mediating role of the impostor phenomenon
items.summary: by Amal Mubarak Alsuwaylim, Bandar A. Alsharif, Mohamed Sayed Abdellatif, Mohammed Rahmath, Ashraf Ragab Ibrahim, Mohamed Ali Nemtallah Despite growing evidence linking academic entitlement to diminished student outcomes, the psychological mechanisms through which entitled academic expectations erode student well-being remain insufficiently understood. The present study examines the mediating role of the impostor phenomenon in the relationship between academic entitlement and well-being among university students. A cross-sectional correlational design was employed with a sample of 864 undergraduate students recruited from Al-Azhar University and Kafr El-Sheikh University in Egypt. Participants completed the Academic Entitlement Scale (AES-28), the Short Clance Impostor Phenomenon Scale (CIPS-10), and the BBC Well-Being Scale (BBC-WBS).
items.author: Amal Mubarak Alsuwaylim, Bandar A. Alsharif, Mohamed Sayed Abdellatif et al.

items.title: Assessment of Pleurotus ostreatus and Pleurotus citrinopileatus mushroom as bioshielding materials for neutron attenuation in medical cyclotron
items.summary: by Md. Jahid Hasan, Md. Nahid Hossain, Hasan Mehdi, Jannatul Ferdous, Md. Shohag Mia, Md. Akhtaruzzaman, Md. Mohi Uddin Neutron absorbance efficiency is crucial for radiation shielding and nuclear reactors, with mushrooms like Pleurotus Ostreatus (PO) and Pleurotus Citrinopleatus (PC) enhancing this property due to their nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, cadmium, and carbon content. Processed into 3 × 3 inch blocks at the National Institute of Nuclear Medicine and Allied Science (NINMAS), the mushrooms are dried at 80°C and ground to powder for analysis. Structural studies using XRD, FESEM, FTIR, and UV-vis spectroscopic reveal high carbon and oxygen levels. For the PO, the XRD investigation showed a broad diffraction peak that corresponded to an estimated crystallite size of about 1.34 nm, while PC showed a mostly amorphous structure devoid of clear crystalline diffraction peaks.
items.author: Md. Jahid Hasan, Md. Nahid Hossain, Hasan Mehdi et al.

items.title: Lifestyle and dietary changes among cancer patients receiving active treatment: A cross-sectional study at a tertiary care center in Lebanon
items.summary: by Solay Farhat, Zeinab Hammoud, Nadeen Zayour, Jinan Fahs, Tasneem Freijeh, Nada Moussaoui, Hawraa Al Rachiini, Bassam Matar Background Cancer diagnosis is often accompanied by changes in nutritional needs and lifestyle habits, which may ultimately be associated with patients’ quality of life (QOL). Despite the high burden of cancer in Lebanon, limited data exist on how dietary intake and lifestyle behaviors change following diagnosis. This study aimed to assess self-reported retrospective changes in dietary and lifestyle behaviors following cancer diagnosis and examine factors associated with these changes and their relationship with QOL. Methods This single-center, cross-sectional study was conducted at Al Zahraa Hospital University Medical Center in Beirut, Lebanon.

items.title: Differential and directional body coupling analysis in Parkinsonian gait
items.summary: by Arifa Zahir, Jaehong Yu, Jin-Sun Jun, Kiwon Park, Ryul Kim, Hyundoo Jeong Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder primarily characterized by motor impairments and altered whole-body coordination. Objective and accessible approaches for quantifying inter-limb and cross-directional coupling during gait remain limited in clinical settings. Using a prospectively collected dataset of individuals with PD and healthy controls (HC), we propose a comprehensive analytical framework based on human pose estimation to extract time-series kinematic signals from key body landmarks. Coupling strengths between body segments were quantified to characterize whole-body coordination patterns. Statistical filtering identified discriminative body coupling factors that significantly differentiated PD from HC.
items.author: Arifa Zahir, Jaehong Yu, Jin-Sun Jun et al.

items.title: Trends in psychotropic drug use in nursing home residents with dementia and their association with regulatory changes: A routine care data analysis from 2016 to 2023
items.summary: by Charlotte A. W. Albers, Fenne Wouters, Martine C. de Bruijne, Martin Smalbrugge, Karlijn J. Joling Introduction Non-pharmacological interventions are the first-choice treatment for managing neuropsychiatric symptoms in nursing home (NH) residents with dementia, yet psychotropic drugs (PDs) are frequently prescribed despite their limited effectiveness. In the current century, policies in various countries have increasingly emphasized the need for restraint in prescribing PDs, partly through amendments to guidelines and legislation. In the Netherlands, regulatory changes included the 2018 revision of the guideline for challenging behavior, the introduction of the Care and Coercion Act (CCA), and a new Dementia Care Standard in 2020.
items.author: Charlotte A. W. Albers, Fenne Wouters, Martine C. de Bruijne et al.

items.title: Health visibility in electoral candidate programs: Insights from the ballot box in an Arab Gulf country
items.summary: by Salman Alzayani, Khaldoon Al-Roomi, Amer Almarabheh, Mohamed Alqahtani Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries face substantial burdens from noncommunicable diseases along with high public expectations of health services, yet little is known about whether health is visibly represented in candidates’ declared election programs in this region. This study examined publicly identifiable candidates’ programs from the Kingdom of Bahrain’s Council of Representatives 2022 elections and assessed among candidates with identifiable programs whether the presence of explicit visible health content and candidates’ characteristics are associated with positive election outcomes. A cross-sectional study was undertaken using the complete cohort of candidates in Bahrain’s 2022 elections (N = 336).
items.author: Salman Alzayani, Khaldoon Al-Roomi, Amer Almarabheh et al.

items.title: Quasi-Normal Modes and thermalization in integrable Quantum Field Theories from the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz
items.summary: We propose a Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) approach for describing thermalization in integrable quantum field theories. The exponential damping and oscillations when approaching thermal equilibrium can be understood as the analogs of quasi-normal mode (QNM) frequencies of black hole perturbations within the framework of holography. Holographic intuitions and some general properties of thermal Green's functions motivate the existence of such a TBA formulation, as well as lead to the imposition of a nonstandard analytical structure on the QNM TBA, while comparison with integrable form-factor expansions fixes the remaining ingredients. We conjecture the QNM TBA to be equivalent to performing an all-order resummation of secular terms in a thermal form factor expansion of retarded 2-point correlation functions.
items.author: Zoltan Bajnok, Romuald A. Janik

items.title: Universally Certifying Partially Self-Correcting Quantum Memories in 3D Translation-Invariant Stabilizer Codes
items.summary: Achieving passive protection of quantum information at finite temperature is a central problem at the intersection of quantum information and quantum many-body physics. Yet a general, computable criterion for determining self-correcting behavior directly from the form of local interactions remains elusive. Here we develop a unified algebraic-geometric framework for certifying partial self-correction in three-dimensional translation-invariant local stabilizer codes, encompassing the cubic code as a special case. From the algebraic curves defined by the codes' defining polynomials, we construct valuation matrices on the boundaries of their normalized projective closures and derive a computable rank criterion. Together with a polynomial-time decoder, this criterion guarantees super-Arrhenius memory lifetimes for code families satisfying it under the specified local Davies dynamics.
items.author: Chong-Yuan Xu, Yong Xu

items.title: Beyond the Gap: What Imaginary-Time Evolution Reveals About the Edge of the Continuum
items.summary: The spectral gap, the energy separating the ground state from the first excitation, governs many quantum phenomena, yet it is far harder to compute than the ground state. We propose a mathematically rigorous method for extracting the gap from imaginary-time evolution in infinite-dimensional Hamiltonians, where the first excitation typically marks the edge of a continuous spectrum. We show that a gap is not automatically detected: detection depends on how the initial state and observable couple the ground state to excitations at the bottom of the continuum. When this coupling follows a power law, the gap is recovered together with a logarithmic correction whose coefficient yields the exponent of the spectral density near the edge of the continuum, which reflects the physics of the excitations.
items.author: Ruben Karapetyan, Denys Bondar, Jakub Mareček et al.

items.title: Helium States in a CAS(2,2) Subspace Inspired by Quantum Photonics
items.summary: We present a four-mode Fock-state photonics implementation of the variational quantum deflation (VQD) algorithm to calculate the ground-state and excited-state energies for the neutral helium atom in a CAS(2,2) Subspace. Its CAS(2,2) electronic Hilbert space is encoded into a bosonic Fock-space representation and subsequently optimized using a continuous-variable quantum circuit. The circuit architecture under study is constructed of single-mode phase shifts, beam splitters, and cross-Kerr interactions. The variational circuit is initialized in the Fock state $\ket{1100}$ and its performance is benchmarked against exact diagonalization of the active-space configuration-interaction (CASCI) Hamiltonian. We also extend the method to optimize from the first to three excited states of the helium atom with the aid of the variational quantum deflation $(VQD)$ method in a CAS(2,2).

items.title: Planting neutrino SE-EdS: A < 3% accurate clustering approximation for neutrinos and other hot dark matter
items.summary: The age of the cosmic neutrino is upon us. Aside from their fundamental importance to particle physics and the recent tensions in their mass scale $M_ν= \sum m_ν$, neutrinos' degeneracies with other cosmological parameters in analyses of scale-dependent cosmic clustering will significantly affect the estimates of these parameters, making accurate, inexpensive, easily-implemented approximations essential tools for theoretical cosmology. We present a new linear approximation, SE-EdS, applicable to non-relativistic neutrinos and other hot dark matter, which is exact in the linear Einstein-de Sitter case, and < 3% accurate for a broad range of flat and non-flat cosmologies characterized by parameters $0.2 \leq Ω_{m,0} \leq 1$, $0 \leq Ω_{ν,0} \leq 0.018$, $-0.1 \leq Ω_{K,0} \leq 0.1$, and $w_0 \leq -0.6$, at all length scales.
items.author: Amol Upadhye, Yvonne Y. Y. Wong

items.title: Constraining Lorentz Invariance Violation via Precision Atomic Spectroscopy
items.summary: This paper investigates Lorentz violation arising from quantum gravity effects in electronic and muonic hydrogen atoms. The violation is modeled through a modified dispersion relation parameterized by a dimensionless coefficient $ξ$ and suppressed by the Planck scale. Using high-precision spectroscopic data and a chi-squared fitting procedure that carefully accounts for theoretical uncertainties in the Rydberg constant and the proton radius, the analysis yields a 95% confidence level constraint $ξ\in [-14.3,\; 1.37] \times 10^5$. The mass scaling of the effect reveals two distinct regimes: for the lowest-order deformation, the heavy nucleus amplifies the signal, while for higher-order corrections, the lepton dominates the sensitivity.

items.title: Kardar--Parisi--Zhang density hydrodynamics in a coherent XXZ--ASEP Lindbladian
items.summary: Coherent interactions can generate quantum correlations without changing a stationary density current. Whether that current still determines long-wavelength transport is a dynamical question. We study an XXZ chain with asymmetric Lindblad hopping, whose stationary current has the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) form although its populations do not evolve autonomously. The current curvature and static susceptibility fix the leading Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) length and amplitude without a fitted length or amplitude conversion factor. The density-visible Liouvillian spectrum, real-space spreading, and Fourier relaxation support KPZ scaling at the finite coherent couplings studied. Central and intermediate stationary density correlations are consistent with the Prähofer--Spohn profile at this microscopic scale, with resolved finite-time corrections.

items.title: Improved Exact and Approximate Quantum Fourier Transforms from Multiplication
items.summary: In the world of quantum computing, quantum Fourier transform (QFT) has been one of the most important subroutines for quantum algorithms, as exemplified by Shor's factoring algorithms and phase estimation (which in itself has been used as a primitive in various quantum algorithms). In fact most of the well known quantum algorithms can be divided into two classes, QFT based algorithms and search based algorithms. The usual circuit for QFT (covered in almost every basic quantum algorithms course) needs $O(q^2)$ gates (and $O(q)$ qubits) to perform the exact Fourier transform over $\mathbb{F}_{2^q}$. Cleve and Watrous (FOCS 2000) improved this gate count to $O(q (\log q)^2 (\log \log q))$ using the integer multiplication algorithm in $O(n (\log n) (\log \log n))$ time for two $n$-bit integers (best known at that time).
